questions.question: Which sentence is an example of negative inversion?

options.A: Never before had I experienced such intense heat.
options.B: I had never experienced such intense heat before.

questions.correct_answer_text: Never before had I experienced such intense heat.

steps: 'Never before had I experienced' inverts the subject and auxiliary after a negative adverbial.

questions.explanation: Inversion is used for emphasis.

questions.question: What is the normal word order of 'Never before had I experienced such intense heat'?

options.A: I had never experienced such intense heat before.
options.B: Had I never experienced heat before.
options.D: I never had experienced heat before.

questions.correct_answer_text: I had never experienced such intense heat before.

steps: In normal order: subject + auxiliary: I had never experienced such intense heat before.
solution.summary: I had never experienced such intense heat before.

questions.explanation: Inversion swaps the subject and auxiliary for emphasis.

questions.question: What do we call it when we begin a sentence with a negative adverbial and invert the subject?

steps: The text calls this 'inversion'.

questions.explanation: We use it to add emphasis.

questions.question: Which words can begin a sentence with inversion?

steps: We begin with negative adverbials such as Seldom and Rarely, or words like Only, So and Such.

questions.explanation: These words trigger inversion.

questions.question: What does 'Little did I realise how differently I would feel about them soon' mean?

options.A: I did not realise at all

questions.correct_answer_text: I did not realise at all

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: 'Little did I realise' means I did not realise at all.
solution.summary: Little did I realise = I did not realise.

questions.explanation: This is inversion after 'little'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses inversion correctly?

options.A: Only when we reached the top did I realise how high the dunes were.
options.B: Only when we reached the top I realised how high the dunes were.
options.C: Only did when we reached the top I realise.
options.D: We reached only the top did I realise.

questions.correct_answer_text: Only when we reached the top did I realise how high the dunes were.

steps: After 'Only when...' the subject and auxiliary are inverted: did I realise.

questions.explanation: The auxiliary 'did' comes before the subject.

questions.question: What is the normal word order of 'Only when we reached the top did I realise how high the dunes were'?

options.A: I only realised how high the dunes were when we reached the top.
options.B: Only I realised when we reached the top.
options.C: I realised only the dunes were high.
options.D: We reached the top and I only realised.

questions.correct_answer_text: I only realised how high the dunes were when we reached the top.

steps: In normal order: I only realised how high the dunes were when we reached the top.
solution.summary: I only realised... when we reached the top.

questions.explanation: Inversion moves 'did' before 'I' for emphasis.

questions.question: Complete: 'Rarely ______ such a crazy experience as a family.'

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: After 'Rarely' we invert: Rarely have we had such a crazy experience.

questions.explanation: Rarely is a negative adverbial, so the auxiliary comes first.

questions.question: In the text, 'Rarely have we had such a crazy experience' means ...

options.A: we have hardly ever had such a crazy experience

questions.correct_answer_text: we have hardly ever had such a crazy experience

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: 'Rarely' = seldom; the family hardly ever has such a crazy experience.

questions.explanation: The dune bashing was extraordinary for them.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'Not only... but also' with correct inversion?

options.A: Not only was it clear that the coach had not been serviced, but also that care had not been taken.
options.B: Not only it was clear that...
options.C: Not only was clear it that...

questions.correct_answer_text: Not only was it clear that the coach had not been serviced, but also that care had not been taken.

steps: With 'Not only' at the start, we invert: Not only was it clear...

questions.explanation: The auxiliary 'was' comes before the subject 'it'.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using inversion?

steps: The text says 'To add emphasis, we can begin sentences with negative adverbials...'

questions.explanation: It makes the sentence sound stronger and more dramatic.

questions.question: Which sentence is a cleft sentence?

options.A: It was the flowing golden dunes which really impressed me.
options.B: The flowing golden dunes impressed me.
options.C: I was impressed by the dunes.

questions.correct_answer_text: It was the flowing golden dunes which really impressed me.

steps: A cleft sentence begins with It's/What and splits the information into two parts.
solution.summary: It was X which... = cleft sentence.

questions.explanation: Cleft sentences make information more memorable.

questions.question: In 'It was the flowing golden dunes which really impressed me', what is emphasised?

steps: The cleft structure 'It was X which...' emphasises X, the dunes.

questions.explanation: The structure puts the important information first.

questions.question: Complete: 'What I was really wild about was ______.'

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: 'What I was really wild about though, was seeing the desert for the first time.'

questions.explanation: The cleft with 'What' emphasises seeing the desert.

questions.question: What do cleft sentences begin with?

options.A: It's, What, The only thing that

questions.correct_answer_text: It's, What, The only thing that

steps: Cleft sentences start with It's and What, and also The (only) thing that, The day when, etc.
solution.summary: It's / What / The only thing that.

questions.explanation: These structures add emphasis.

questions.question: Complete: 'What you can expect is good food, fast cars and great ______.'

steps: The advert says 'What you can expect is good food, fast cars and great roads.'

questions.explanation: This is from the Jordan Rally advert.

questions.question: Complete: 'What you'll find amazing is the ______.'

steps: The advert says 'What you'll find amazing is the camaraderie.'

questions.explanation: Camaraderie means friendship between people.

questions.question: What does 'camaraderie' mean?

steps: 'Camaraderie' means friendship and mutual trust, especially among a group.

questions.explanation: A passion for cars unites the group.

questions.question: Complete: 'It's the camaraderie ______ amazing.'

steps: 'It's the camaraderie that's amazing.'

questions.explanation: The cleft structure is It's X that's Y.

questions.question: Rewrite the cleft sentence 'It's the camaraderie that's amazing' using 'What'. What would it be?

options.A: What you'll find amazing is the camaraderie.

questions.correct_answer_text: What you'll find amazing is the camaraderie.

steps: The 'What' cleft version: What you'll find amazing is the camaraderie.
solution.summary: What you'll find amazing is the camaraderie.

questions.explanation: Both versions emphasise the same information.

questions.question: Complete the inversion: 'He never felt sorry for himself. → NOT ONCE ______ sorry for himself.'

steps: With 'Not once' at the start, invert: Not once did he feel sorry for himself.
solution.summary: Not once did he feel sorry for himself.

questions.explanation: Negative adverbial + inversion.

questions.question: Complete the inversion: 'He didn't know what was going to happen. → LITTLE ______ what was going to happen.'

steps: With 'Little' at the start: Little did he know what was going to happen.

questions.explanation: 'Little' here is a negative adverbial.

questions.question: Complete the inversion: 'She was so happy that she thought she would never stop smiling. → SO ______ that she thought she would never stop smiling.'

steps: With 'So' at the start: So happy was she that she thought she would never stop smiling.

questions.explanation: The complement 'happy' moves before the verb.

questions.question: Complete the inversion: 'The speed was so great that they started to feel scared. → SUCH ______ that they started to feel scared.'

steps: With 'Such' at the start: Such was the speed that they started to feel scared.

questions.explanation: 'Such' + inverted be-verb.

questions.question: What is the text 'Speeding in the sand' about?

options.A: a family trying dune bashing in the desert

questions.correct_answer_text: a family trying dune bashing in the desert

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: The text is about a family's first experience of dune bashing.

questions.explanation: They surged up the dunes in a special car.

questions.question: What is 'dune bashing'?

options.A: driving over sand dunes in a special vehicle

questions.correct_answer_text: driving over sand dunes in a special vehicle

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: They went dune bashing in a car especially equipped for the sport.

questions.explanation: It is a thrilling desert activity.

questions.question: What did the writer's father say the experience was like?

options.A: a rollercoaster without the feeling of safety
options.B: a boat trip in a storm
options.D: a theme park ride with seatbelts

questions.correct_answer_text: a rollercoaster without the feeling of safety

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: Dad said it was like a rollercoaster without the feeling of safety.

questions.explanation: Everyone agreed with him.

questions.question: What does 'we got a real kick out of it' mean?

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: 'Get a kick out of something' means to enjoy it a lot.
solution.summary: got a kick out of it = really enjoyed it.

questions.explanation: They loved the high speeds and scenery.

questions.question: Where was the writer when they went dune bashing?

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: The family arrived in Dubai on holiday and then went to the desert.
solution.summary: They went to the desert near Dubai.

questions.explanation: It was the writer's first time in the Middle East.

questions.question: What was the guide's name?

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: The text says 'we set off with our guide, Saeed'.

questions.explanation: He took them to a car equipped for the sport.

questions.question: Complete the cleft sentence: '______ the camaraderie that's amazing.'

steps: 'It's the camaraderie that's amazing.'

questions.explanation: The cleft begins with 'It's'.

questions.question: Which structure is NOT used to begin a cleft sentence?

steps: Clefts begin with It's, What, The (only) thing that, The day when, etc.; 'Never before' starts an inversion.

questions.explanation: The others are all cleft starters.

questions.question: Complete: 'The day when I learnt how to use cleft sentences was the best day of my life!' What does this cleft sentence emphasise?

steps: 'The day when...' emphasises the day itself.

questions.explanation: 'The day when' is one of the cleft starters.

questions.question: Which word can begin an inversion meaning 'not very often'?

steps: 'Seldom' and 'Rarely' are negative adverbials meaning not often.

questions.explanation: With them we invert the subject.

questions.question: What did the writer's mother do during the dune bashing ride?

options.A: she laughed in fear for the entire ride

questions.correct_answer_text: she laughed in fear for the entire ride

source.reference: Reading text: Speeding in the sand

steps: 'Mum just laughed in fear for the entire ride.'

questions.explanation: The ride was scary but thrilling for her.

questions.question: Complete: 'Only when the lights went out ______ how dark it was.'

steps: After 'Only when...', invert: Only when the lights went out did I realise.

questions.explanation: Inversion follows the negative adverbial phrase.

questions.question: Which sentence is written in normal (non-inverted) word order?

options.A: The coach was half an hour late.
options.B: Never have I experienced such discomfort.
options.C: Little did he know the truth.
options.D: So cold was the water that we left.

questions.correct_answer_text: The coach was half an hour late.

steps: 'The coach was half an hour late' follows normal subject + verb order.

questions.explanation: The others all start with negative adverbials or 'So'.

questions.question: What is the effect of using a cleft sentence like 'It was Dad who said it was like a rollercoaster'?

options.A: it makes the sentence more emphatic and memorable
options.B: it makes the sentence longer for no reason

questions.correct_answer_text: it makes the sentence more emphatic and memorable

steps: Cleft sentences emphasise information and make it sound more memorable.

questions.explanation: The focus is put on 'Dad'.

questions.question: Complete the inversion with 'Not until': 'Not until the train arrived ______ that we were late.'

steps: After 'Not until...', invert: Not until the train arrived did we realise that we were late.

questions.explanation: 'Not until' is a negative expression that causes inversion.

questions.question: Which pair of sentences mean the same: 'What impressed me most was the desert' and ...

steps: 'What impressed me most was the desert' equals 'The desert impressed me most', with emphasis added.
solution.summary: Both mean the desert impressed me most.

questions.explanation: The cleft adds emphasis to the desert.
